title: "Gjergj Kastrioti Skënderbeu" Decoration
text:
"Gjergj Kastrioti Skënderbeu" Decoration
"Gjergj Kastrioti Skënderbeu" Decoration
For the order that was founded in 1925, see
Order of Skanderbeg (1925–1945)
.
"Gjergj Kastrioti Skënderbeu" Decoration
Awarded by the
President of Albania
Type
State decoration
Eligibility
Albanians
,
foreign nationals
[
1
]
Awarded for
Important contributions or specific heroic acts for the defense, strengthening and advancement of the Republic of Albania
Status
Currently constituted
Head
President of Albania
The
"Gjergj Kastrioti Skënderbeu" Decoration
(
Albanian
:
Dekorata "Gjergj Kastrioti Skënderbeu"
) is a high honorary
state decoration
that is currently awarded to Albanian and foreign citizens in Albania, that have made an important contribution to the defence, reinforcement and development of the Republic of Albania.
[
2
]
[
3
]
The name refers to
Skanderbeg
, who is the
national hero
of the
Albanian people
. The Decoration is granted by the
President of Albania
. It should not be confused with the royal
Order of Skanderbeg
, which is a
dynastic order
bestowed by the
Albanian royal family
.
Recipients
Some recipients to date include:
[
4
]
Sabah Al-Ahmad Al-Jaber Al-Sabah
,
Emir
of
Kuwait
(decorated on 27 May 2012) for his financial contribution to the reconstruction of the
Skanderbeg Square
.
[
5
]
Anthony Bailey
, Irish interfaith campaigner.
[
6
]
Laura Boldrini
, President of the
Chamber of Deputies of Italy
.
[
7
]
Henry Brooke
, retired British
Court of Appeal
judge.
[
8
]
Rudolf Decker (politician, former Member of the
Landtag of Baden-Württemberg
, and Chair of the
Vereinigung für Grundwerte und Völkerverständigung
["Foundation for Basic Values and International Understanding"] (awarded by President
Bujar Nishani
in June 2017).
Rosemary DiCarlo
, American diplomat.
[
9
]
Yuli Edelstein
, Israeli politician.
[
10
]
Sabri Godo
, writer, screenwriter, politician (posthumously decorated by President of Albania Bujar Nishani on 12 December 2012).
[
11
]
Azem Hajdari
, assassinated Albanian politician (decorated posthumously by proposal of President
Bamir Topi
on 10 September 2008).
Sabri Hamiti
(decorated on 10 May 2010) for
the irreplaceable contribution to modern Albanian thought and for the role played in facing the historical challenges that the Albanian people faced in the late 20th century
.
[
12
]
Ramush Haradinaj
, former Prime Minister of Kosovo.
[
13
]
Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani
, Emir of
Qatar
(decorated by President Bamir Topi on 18 October 2011).
[
14
]
Jonathan M. Moore
, U.S. Diplomat, (awarded by President
Bujar Nishani
28 November 2014)
[
15
]
Fatos Nano
, former
Prime Minister of Albania
(decorated by proposal of President
Alfred Moisiu
).
Giorgio Napolitano
, President of the
Republic of Italy
(2014).
Doris Pack
, German politician, President of EPP Women and former Member of the European Parliament 1989–2014.
[
16
]
Colin Powell
, retired US General, former
Secretary of State
(decorated on 1 May 2003 by proposal of President Alfred Moisiu).
Fatmir Sejdiu
, President of
Kosovo
(decorated by President Bamir Topi on 3 November 2008).
Ismail Serageldin
, Vice President of the
World Bank
(1992–2000), Emeritus Librarian of the
Bibliotheca Alexandrina
.
[
17
]
Michael Spindelegger
, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Austria (2008–2013)
Aleksandar Stipčević
,
Croatian-Albanian
historian and archaeologist.
[
18
]
Cafo Beg Ulqini
, former
Mayor of Ulqin
, Leader of
Second League of Prizren
(decorated by proposal of President
Bujar Nishani
in April 2016).
[
19
]
Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan
,
UAE
Foreign Minister (decorated by President of Albania Bujar Nishani on 14 March 2014).
[
20
]
Xhevahir Spahiu
(decorated February 2020) for his contribution to the national culture.
[
21
]
RAI
Kalabria (decorated 21 October 2023): for their significant contribution to preserving the
Arbëreshë
culture and language.

22
]
